final:
I didn't build or solve a spec for this brief, because the arm can't be held still as described.

The only support is one hinge pin along z at (x = 10, y = 20) that turns freely. A pin like that stops the arm from moving in x and y, but nothing stops it rotating about z. The 400 N downward load at x = 200 sits 190 mm from the pin, so it puts 400 N × 190 mm = 76 000 N·mm of moment about the pin. Nothing in the brief pushes back against that moment, so the arm would just swing down around the pin. With no static equilibrium, the stiffness problem has no solution.

I didn't model the pin as a fully fixed cylinder of nodes. The solver would accept that, but it would quietly turn the free hinge into a clamp, which contradicts the brief.

To make the problem solvable, the brief needs one more support that resists rotation, for example:
- a second pin or a stop somewhere along the arm;
- a clamped pin instead of a free hinge;
- a tie or strut at the far end.

REFUSE: a single freely turning hinge pin can't resist the 76 000 N·mm moment the far-end load puts on it, so the arm has a rigid rotation about z and can't be held still.
